layers.note: Shares the canopy with Douglas-fir on moist ground and fills the understory beneath it.

moisture.note: Commonest on moist to wet ground (seeps, stream bottoms, swamps, lower slopes); tolerates saturated soil better than Douglas-fir, but not standing water.

heat_load.note: Favours cool, moist aspects and shaded ravines; scarce on hot south-west slopes.

elevation_m.note: Lowlands to about 1,200 m in western Washington.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on slopes but most often on benches, bottoms and toe slopes.

shade_tolerance.note: Very shade tolerant: seedlings and saplings persist under closed canopy.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −6 °C, gone by −12 °C, up to about 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −30 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −38 °C.

warmest_c.note: Cool to warm summers: warmest-month means from about 13.5 to 23.5 °C; below 11 °C summers are too short for it and above 27 °C too hot.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 550: the warmth of the maritime lowlands and lower mountain slopes.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.6, gone by 0.45.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in western Washington lowland forests; not yet checked against Silvics of North America (Burns and Honkala, 1990) or the Fire Effects Information System, both public-domain USDA Forest Service works. Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Western redcedar grows from south-east Alaska to north-west California near the coast, and inland in the wet belt of British Columbia, Idaho and Montana (Silvics of North America, vol. 1). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
